beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open (portrait). Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Aloha, this is Liam, in for Bear. Today we tear down the skill every other explainer inherits from — the one just called `explainer`. Not the AI cut, not the CLI cut, not the deep cut. The parent. What is it, really? And how does it decide what ends up on screen? Here is the mental model.

show.event: composer card fades in on cream
greeting 'Aloha, Liam' types above the composer

props.command: What is the `explainer` skill? Read skills/make/explainer/SKILL.md and tell me what it actually is.
output: it is a compositing PIPELINE, not a style
the still must be evidence, not texture

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer corrects 'style' into 'pipeline'. Portrait uses larger font and more lines to fill 1080×1920 safe area.
beats.narration_text: The easy mistake — the one every fellow makes first — is thinking Vox is a look. Cream paper, editorial serif, hand-drawn ring. It is not. Vox is a pipeline. It laundered any source you throw at it — an archive photo, a Manim fragment, a public-domain reel — through one treatment. Sources never match. The treatment does. That is why the film reads as one film.

beats.role_note: Pipeline — four phases in portrait. 4 phases + input + output = 6 nodes, fits portrait width.
beats.narration_text: Here is the pipeline. Script becomes beats. Beats become a Kokoro voiceover — free, local, and the master clock. Then media flows in per beat from four sources: Manim fragments, treated stills over Ken Burns, public-domain footage, and Remotion annotations. Compile conforms every slot to the audio window and hands out one watchable master. That is the whole loop. Anything else is a modifier on top of it.

show.event: title 'One clock. Four sources.' fades in
four phase nodes reveal, 'audio' lit terracotta

props.title: One clock. Four sources.
props.footerNote: Every beat is a per-beat mp4. Nothing gets baked before the audio is measured.

beats.role_note: DESIGN · TELL — VOX LAW. A still is EVIDENCE, never texture.
beats.narration_text: Here is where the skill bites. VOX LAW: a still exists for exactly one reason — the still IS the evidence. The actual record the argument turns on. The updated skill adds a sharper edge. If your evidence is locally reproducible — a table, a chart, a test run, code output — execute it and render it. A terminal photograph is decoration. The running output is the evidence. Princeton's actual admissions record — yes. A stock photo of a university — no. The test: could this still be swapped for any other still of the same subject without changing what the beat proves? If yes, it is decoration. Cut it.

props.heading: A still is evidence.
props.body: New in the updated skill (EXECUTABLE-EVIDENCE.md): if your evidence is locally reproducible — code output, a table, a chart, a test run — execute it and render the result. A terminal photograph is decoration; the running output is the evidence. Swap test: could this still be replaced by any other still of the same subject? If YES, cut it.
props.quote: There is no share to hit… any prior guidance stating a target percentage of vox body beats is superseded by this law.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. The explainer skill is the chassis every other explainer bolts onto. It is a compositing pipeline, not a style. The Kokoro voiceover is the master clock, and free. The two-axis shot system separates presentation from provenance so swaps stay cheap. The slot contract makes the first pass a watchable film with slates. And VOX LAW keeps every still that reaches the timeline load-bearing. Do this well, and mixed media reads as one film. Break the last rule, and you shipped a slide show.

artifactLines: explainer is the chassis. AI-, CLI-, deep-explainer all inherit it verbatim.
Kokoro is the master clock — free, local, and the reason nothing waits.
shot.type is locked at plan gate; shot.source is late-bound so swaps stay free.
VOX LAW: a still is EVIDENCE, never texture. If it swaps, cut it.
First pass is always a watchable film — slates are a request, not a defect.
